questions.problem: Let $A(1,0,-1)$ and $B(0,1,1).$ Find $|a+2b|,$ where $a$ and $b$ are position vectors of $A$ and $B$, respectively.
questions.worked_solution:
We have 

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{OA}=a=i-k, \\  & \overset{\to }{OB}=b=j+k.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the coordinates of $a+2b$, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}a+2b & =(i-k)+2(j+k) \\  & =i+2j+k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|a+2b| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+4+1} \\  & =\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $A(5,0,9)$ and $B(3,9,8).$ Find $|a-b|,$ where $a$ and $b$ are position vectors of $A$ and $B$, respectively.
questions.worked_solution:
We have 

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{OA}=a=5i+9k, \\  & \overset{\to }{OB}=b=3i+9j+8k.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the coordinates of $a-b$, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}a-b & =(5i+9k)-(3i+9j+8k) \\  & =2i-9j+k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|a-b| & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-9)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+81+1} \\  & =\sqrt{86}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{OA}=a=2i+j, \\  & \overset{\to }{OB}=b=i+3j-3k.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the coordinates of $a+2b$, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}a+2b & =(2i+j)+2(i+3j-3k) \\  & =4i+7j-6k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|a+2b| & =\sqrt{(4)^{2}+(7)^{2}+(-6)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+49+36} \\  & =\sqrt{101}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $a=⟨-2,8,3⟩.$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $a.$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
u=\frac{a}{|\,a\,|}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,a\,| & =\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}+{a}_{z}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{8}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+64+9} \\  & =\sqrt{77}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $a$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{a}{|\,a\,|} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{77}}a \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{77}}\cdot ⟨-2,8,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{2}{\sqrt{77}},\frac{8}{\sqrt{77}},\frac{3}{\sqrt{77}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given that $c=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$, find a unit vector that is parallel to $c.$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
u=\frac{c}{|\,c\,|}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,c\,| & =\sqrt{{c}_{x}^{2}+{c}_{y}^{2}+{c}_{z}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $c$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{c}{|\,c\,|} \\  & =\frac{1}{1}c \\  & =1\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{OA}=a=5i-j+k, \\  & \overset{\to }{OB}=b=-2j+3k.\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing $\overset{\to }{AB}$ as the difference of position vectors, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =\overset{\to }{OB}-\overset{\to }{OA} \\  & =b-a \\  & =(-2j+3k)-(5i-j+k) \\  & =-5i-j+2k.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\overset{\to }{AB}| & =\sqrt{(-5)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25+1+4} \\  & =\sqrt{30}.\end{aligned}

questions.problem: Let $A(2,7,0)$ and $B(2,5,4).$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $\overset{\to }{AB}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{OA}=a=2i+7j, \\  & \overset{\to }{OB}=b=2i+5j+4k.\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing $\overset{\to }{AB}$ as the difference of position vectors, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =\overset{\to }{OB}-\overset{\to }{OA} \\  & =b-a \\  & =2i+5j+4k-(2i+7j) \\  & =-2j+4k \\  & =⟨0,-2,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
u=\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}}{|\,\overset{\to }{AB}\,|}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,\overset{\to }{AB}\,| & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+4+16} \\  & =\sqrt{20} \\  & =2\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $\overset{\to }{AB}$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}}{|\,\overset{\to }{AB}\,|} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}\overset{\to }{AB} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}\cdot ⟨0,-2,4⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}},\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $R(5,-3,2)$ and $S(1,-1,4).$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $\overset{\to }{SR}.$

$u=⟨${{field-1}}$,\,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}},$
{{field-2}}$⟩$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OR} & =r=5i-3j+2k, \\ \overset{\to }{OS} & =s=i-j+4k.\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing $\overset{\to }{SR}$ as the difference of position vectors, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{SR} & =\overset{\to }{OR}-\overset{\to }{OS} \\  & =r-s \\  & =(5i-3j+2k)-(i-j+4k) \\  & =4i-2j-2k \\  & =⟨4,-2,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
u=\frac{\overset{\to }{SR}}{|\,\overset{\to }{SR}\,|}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\overset{\to }{SR}| & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+4+4} \\  & =2\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $\overset{\to }{SR}$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{\overset{\to }{SR}}{|\,\overset{\to }{SR}\,|} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{6}}\overset{\to }{SR} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{6}}\cdot ⟨4,-2,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}},\,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}},\,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Let $[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $\mathbf{a}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\mathbf{u} = \dfrac{\mathbf{a}}{|\,\mathbf{a}\,|}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,a\,| & =\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}+{a}_{z}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+(-5)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+25+1} \\  & =\sqrt{42}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $\mathbf{a}$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{a}{|\,a\,|} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{42}}a \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{42}}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ -5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4/\sqrt{42} \\ -5/\sqrt{42} \\ 1/\sqrt{42}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
